text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The overall volume of loans totalled 369.7 billion crowns at the end of November last year, a 19-percent increase against the beginning of the year. Crown credits totalled 329.6 billion , some 14.4 percent more than in January 1996, while loans extended in hard currencies totalled 40.1 billion crowns, an increase of 76.6 percent.
- State subsidies for restructuring company debts are expected to total some 70 billion crowns over the next three years.
- Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said privatisation of alluminium producer ZSNP Ziar nad Hronom would only be possible after company's 3.2 billion crown debt restructuring problem.
- Some 254,000 passangers flew from Bratislava airport in 1996, more than 30-percent more than in the previous year.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Privatisation of Slovak banks should be completed as soon as possible, but not later than by the end of this year, said Pavol Kacic, a member of the Presidium of the National Property Fund - the state privatisation agency.

- Chemical company Chemosvit Svit said it had acquired majority control over the Ukraine's Luckplastmas, where it wants to produce plastic foils. Chemosvit's investments in Ukraine are expected to total some $3.0 million over the next two years.

SME - The National Bank of Slovakia admitted it was surprised by sudden changes in the management of the third largest commercial bank IRB a.s., initiated last week by the bank's majority owner, steel producer VSZ Kosice.
- The opposition Democratic Union said the planned Slovak national airline will be majority controlled by Russian shareholders.
